basis: Red-cell aplasia defines DBA12; ventricular septal defect and triphalangeal thumb each reported in 1/1 patients; frequency estimates are limited by the single case.
Inherited ATPase enzymopathy causing anemia; no evidence supplied for damage outside erythrocyte metabolism.
Medulloblastoma is a primary CNS malignancy; molecular subtype does not establish another organ axis.
Defined by a congenital spinal cord-to-skin fibroneural connection and associated cutaneous lesion.
Permanent fetal or infant brain injury causes motor and developmental dysfunction; motor impairment does not establish primary muscle disease.
The syndrome is defined by progressive hearing loss and cataract.
Umbrella of inherited mitochondrial transport disorders; no additional damaged organ is established across most subtypes.
Named inherited deficiency of a deoxyribose-phosphate metabolic enzyme; supplied record does not establish additional organ damage.
Progressive limb-girdle skeletal muscle degeneration; definition explicitly excludes cardiac and oculo-facial-bulbar muscle involvement.
Isolated congenital absence of the tongue affects an oral structure within the gastrointestinal axis.
Trisomy 21 defines a neurodevelopmental syndrome; congenital heart malformations occur in approximately 40-50%; leukemia and thyroid disease are separate diagnoses.
WNT2B-related congenital intestinal disease causes diarrhea in 20/20 patients, with villous atrophy and failure to thrive.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability in 7/7; seizures in 5/7. Hypotonia does not establish muscle damage; premature adrenarche alone is insufficient.
Congenital failure of aortic and pulmonary outflow separation; pulmonary arterial abnormalities are cardiovascular, and lung abnormalities occur in <30%.
Hearing impairment in 6/7 and pulmonary artery stenosis in 5/7 define functional organ disease; posterior embryotoxon in 7/7 is generally a non-impairing ocular marker.
Primary gastric adenocarcinoma confined to gastric mucosa or submucosa; possible nodal spread does not establish another axis.
Hereditary pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma predisposition defines the endocrine axis; renal carcinoma is a separate tumor risk, not intrinsic renal damage.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent infections are separately diagnosed diseases. Bronchiectasis and malabsorption are annotated at <30%.
Brain disorder defined by recurrent abnormal neuronal discharges; no other organ damage applies across the epilepsy umbrella.
Bilirubin metabolism disorder; elevated circulating bilirubin alone does not establish liver injury, hemolysis, or neurologic damage.
Adenocarcinoma originates in a uterine ligament, a reproductive support structure outside the locomotor musculoskeletal axis.
Congenital transposition and coarctation are structural abnormalities of the heart and great arteries.
Malignancy directly occupies limb bone; no additional organ involvement is established.
Postinfectious immune inflammation; cardiac dysfunction occurs in >30%, and inflammatory GI involvement is common (~60-90%) and a major diagnostic category; transient rash excluded.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and progressive visual loss affect most patients over the typical course.
